name: Gayā
location: On the Phalgu river. Lat. 24°48', long. 85°1'
about: The famous pitṛ-tīrtha, where the lotus feet of Śrī Gadādhara (Viṣṇu) are present; what is offered here in śrāddha is endless. To see: Gayāśira, Rāmaśilā, Pretaśilā, Brahmakuṇḍa, Dhenuka-tīrtha, Yonidvāra, Phalgu-tīrtha. There are 45 vedīs or tīrthas. The Viṣṇupada temple was built by Rāṇī Ahalyābāī for nine lakh rupees; on the Rāmaśilā hill are temples of Mahādeva and Pārvatī; the strange cave on the Brahmayoni hill is called «Bhīma Gayā». Its glories are told in the Vāyu-purāṇa, the Mahābhārata and the Harivaṁśa. Sanctified by the feet of Śrī Gaura and Nityānanda (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 17.8, Caitanya-bhāgavata Ādi).

name: Vārāṇasī
aka: Varanasi, Benares, Kāśī, Kasi, Kashi, Kāśī-dhāma
location: On the Gaṅgā, where the Varaṇā and the Asi meet it
about: Śrī Kāśī-dhāma. To see: the Viśveśvara temple, Veṇīmādhava, Jñānavāpī, Annapūrṇā, Maṇikarṇikā, Daśāśvamedha, Hariścandra's ghāṭ, and the homestead of Tapana Miśra. The name comes from the meeting of the two rivers Varaṇā and Asi.

name: Prayāga
location: At Allahabad, at the meeting of the Gaṅgā, the Yamunā and the Sarasvatī
about: The king of tīrthas, at the confluence of the Gaṅgā, Yamunā and Sarasvatī. Sanctified by the feet of Śrī Gaura and Nityānanda (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 9, Caitanya-bhāgavata Ādi). (Also the name of a ghāṭ on the Yamunā in Mathurā, and the Daśāśvamedha-ghāṭ at Prayāga.)

name: Kūrmasthāna
location: Eight miles east of Chicacole station (South Eastern Railway)
about: The foremost tīrtha of the Telugu people, sanctified by the feet of Śrī Gaura and Nityānanda (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 7). In the temple is Śrī Kūrmadeva, the tortoise form, with Śrī and Bhū-devī on either side. The temple was in the care of a Mādhva maṭha under the kings of Vijayanagara; an inscription of nine verses records the building of a temple for Yogānanda Nṛsiṁha before Kūrmadeva. It is said that when Rāmānuja was thrown to Kūrmācala by Jagannātha, he took the Kūrma form for a Śiva form and fasted a day, then knew it to be Viṣṇu and began his service (Prapannāmṛta 36).

name: Jiyaḍa-nṛsiṁha
location: «Siṁhācalam» station, five miles north of Vizagapatam (South Eastern Railway); the temple is high on the hill
about: The temple of Śrī Nṛsiṁha high on the hill; ground sanctified by the feet of Śrī Gaura and Nityānanda (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 8). An inscription says that a devout queen of the third Gaṅga king covered the deity with gold. The festival image stays outside and the main deity inside; the service is by followers of Rāmānuja.

name: Śrī Raṅgam
location: On an island of the Kāverī
about: The temple of Śrī Raṅganātha (one of the «five Nāthas»: Badrīnātha, Raṅganātha, Jagannātha, Dvārakānātha and Śrīnātha), with its concentric enclosures and streets. In the time of Sudarśanācārya the Muslims attacked the Raṅganātha temple and killed twelve thousand Śrī Vaiṣṇavas; Raṅganātha was taken to Tirupati, and later Goppaṇārya brought him to Siṁhadurga, where he stayed three years, and in 1293 Śaka he was installed again at Śrīraṅga-kṣetra. A verse by Vedānta Deśika on the east wall of the temple records it.

name: Uḍupī
location: 37 miles from Mangalore, on the bank of the Pāpanāśinī
about: The deity of Śrī Uḍupī-kṛṣṇa, installed by Śrī Madhvācārya: the first of all Kṛṣṇa deities, installed by Arjuna at Dvārakā. When the land by Dvārakā went into the sea, many centuries later Madhvācārya found him inside a boat loaded with gopī-candana.

name: Paṇḍharapura
location: On the Bhīmā river, 38 miles west of Śolāpura; Paṇḍharapura station on a branch of the Bombay–Puṇā–Kurduvāḍī–Raichur line
about: The two-armed Nārāyaṇa: Śrī Viṭhobā. The devotee Puṇḍarīka founded this dhāma. In the 15th Śaka century the famous Vaiṣṇava saint Tukārāma lived here, and also Nāmadeva, Rākā-Bāṅkā, Narahari and other saints. Here Śaṅkarāraṇya attained perfection. Sanctified by the feet of Śrī Gaura (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 9.299–300).

name: Rāmeśvara
location: Four miles north of Pamban port; Rāmeśvaram station, near Rāmanād. Lat. 9°8', long. 79°18'
about: Ground sanctified by the feet of Śrī Gaura and Nityānanda (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 9, Caitanya-bhāgavata Ādi). Dhanuṣkoṭi-tīrtha, one of its twenty-four tīrthas, is 12 miles south-east. To see: Lakṣmaṇa-tīrtha, Sītā-tīrtha, Rāma-tīrtha and the Rāmeśvara temple. Festivals: Śivarātri, Vaiśākha pūrṇimā and others.
